sections.content: How many people stayed in Deal after gaining qualifications?

Deal is a medium-sized town in the South East. Deal does not have its own university.

Deal has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Deal ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 1,470 state-school pupils from Deal who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 420 (29%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 425 (29%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Deal to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Deal's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Deal in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Deal move to?

Of Deal's graduates, 180 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Deal's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 125 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 25 of those qualified non-graduates (20%) were living fairly locally, in the Margate and Ramsgate travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Deal's GCSE cohort:

  • 100 graduates left the South East
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 30 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the South East

In 2018 to 2019, 19% of graduates and 22% of qualified non-graduates living in Deal had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 290 graduates and 385 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Deal. This is compared with the 420 graduates and 425 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 81% of the graduates had also lived in Deal as GCSE pupils, while 19% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Deal in 2018 to 2019, 78% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 22% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
